meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-28 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes | Redwood: Liam Patel (AE), Priya Nair (SE), Jess Park (CSM) | Acme Financial: Carlos Mendes, Rina Gupta, Jamal Thompson, Ava Li
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize focusing on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) and quality-vs-latency tradeoffs for Acme Financial's transaction-classification workload. SE demoed the console profile picker, showed model-level latency/quality curves, and discussed fallback policies and KV cache interactions. Customer expressed concerns about tail latency, hallucination risk with lower-precision quant, and regulatory logging. Agreed to run a pilot benchmark with three profiles and share results + security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll kick off in a sec, um quick intro from our side, I'm Liam Patel AE at Redwood, Priya our SE will run the optimize walkthrough.
[00:18] Carlos: hey thanks, Carlos Mendes here, head of ML at Acme, we've got Rina and Jamal and Ava on the call too.
[00:30] Priya: great, ok so goal for today is to show the quantization profiles in the Optimize tab and walk through INT8 and FP8 tradeoffs, like quality vs latency for your use case. we'll leave time at the end for security questions.
[00:45] Rina: perfect, our main concern is tail latency for inference on short transaction texts, and how much quality we lose when we push to int8/ fp eight.
[00:58] Priya: totally, we'll show the nvbench style curves and an A/B of a few prompts. quick note, transcription might show FP eight as "FP eight" or "fp eight" in the console, apologies for the auto caption crumbs.
[01:12] Jess: also we'll share the benchmarking spreadsheet and the config we used, you'll get the exact prompts and seeds.
[01:25] Jamal: what's the expected SLO delta if we go from fp32 to fp8 on a 16k context? like ballpark.
[01:35] Priya: ballpark depends a lot on sequence length and batch. for short sequences (under 128 tokens) we've seen 30-50% token throughput improvement with FP8 on a single GPU compared to FP32, and INT8 can be similar but sometimes slightly faster depending on kernel support. but quality is the tricky bit.
[01:52] Carlos: by quality you mean accuracy on classification or hallucinations?
[01:58] Priya: both — for your classification workload we measure top-1 label accuracy and soft-label calibration. FP8 tends to preserve accuracy very well on decoder-only models, INT8 sometimes introduces mild degradation on edge cases unless you use a per-channel symmetric quant or a calibration profile.
[02:18] Rina: can you show that in the console?
[02:23] Priya: yeah jumping in now. [screen share] here is the Optimize > Quantization Profiles page. you can see predefined profiles: fp32 baseline, fp8-default, int8-symmetric, int8-asymmetric, and a safety profile that keeps critical layers in fp16.
[02:40] [02:41] Priya: here's the latency vs quality plot we ran with your sample dataset — x-axis latency median ms, y-axis delta accuracy vs baseline. each point is a profile. see fp8 is near the top left — much lower latency with negligible accuracy drop (~0.5%). INT8-symmetric saved slightly more latency but accuracy drops ~1.7% on long-tail cases.
[02:59] Carlos: ok that tail sounds concerning, we need 99th percentile under 200ms end-to-end. what portion of that is runtime vs network?
[03:12] Priya: good question. runtime we can get down to 30-80ms depending on batch and model size on Redwood Dedicated. network and prefix cache hit rates are big factors — if you have a high prefix reuse, KV cache will cut generation time dramatically. note: sometimes transcripts say "KV cash" but it's cache.
[03:33] Rina: our prefix reuse is low for these short transactions, so cache won't help much, we mostly care about per-request latency.
[03:41] Priya: then int8 may be attractive if you can tolerate the small accuracy hit; but we recommend a hybrid profile: keep attention & embeddings in fp16/fp32 and quantize MLPs to int8 — that's what our "safety" preset does.
[03:57] Jamal: how do you validate hallucination risk? any eval hooks?
[04:03] Priya: yes, Optimize has eval sets and quality monitors. you can upload labeled prompt sets and we compute accuracy/regression alerts when switching profiles. we also do per-route rollouts so you can canary FP8 to 5% traffic and monitor metrics.
[04:20] Carlos: that rollout feature is key, we can't just flip a switch across production.
[04:25] Liam: exactly — and we record token-level cost and latencies in the Console for the canary.
[04:31] Ava: security question — does quantization affect payload logging or encryption? we need audit logs and KMS integration.
[04:39] Jess: no effect on encryption; logging is at the request/response level pre/post-inference, and you can opt to redact or disable transcript storage. Redwood Private + Dedicated supports customer KMS and HSM integrations for keys. we'll share the SOC2 pack.
[04:56] Rina: what about model fallback? if int8 starts showing drift, can we auto-fallback to fp16?
[05:03] Priya: yes, we support automatic fallback policies by error/latency thresholds — route-based. you can configure it to fallback to fp16 or a larger model variant.
[05:12] [05:13] Priya: now i'll run a quick live example — same prompt across three profiles: baseline fp32, fp8-default, and int8-symmetric.
[05:22] [05:25] Priya: prompt: "Classify transaction: 'Payment to ACME Corp 12/12 $120.00' — label: fraud / legit". running...
[05:38] [05:40] fp32 result: legit (confidence 0.98) — latency 112ms.
[05:46] fp8 result: legit (confidence 0.96) — latency 72ms.
[05:52] int8 result: legit (confidence 0.88) — latency 60ms.
[05:58] Carlos: ok that's promising but the confidence drop on int8 is not great for borderline cases.
[06:04] Priya: agreed — that's why we calibrate with a representative prompt set. our suggestion: run a 1k sample evaluation and set a minimum confidence threshold and monitor regressions.
[06:16] Rina: how do we run that benchmark? what's the easiest path?
[06:20] Priya: we can run it for you as part of a pilot — Priya (SE) will spin up a dedicated job, run FP32/FP8/INT8 variants, and produce the spreadsheet with accuracy deltas, latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), and token cost. you'll get the raw logs and the aggregated charts.
[06:36] Liam: i'll coordinate scheduling — we typically ask for a 1k prompt set and a few representative longer prompts to understand tails.
[06:44] Jamal: any infra changes on our side for dedicated or private?
[06:48] Liam: Dedicated needs minimal changes — we provision GPU pools. Private requires VPC peering or on-prem infra and a private control plane. we'll share the deployment checklist.
[06:58] Carlos: curious about quantization tooling — is it done during model load or ahead of time? runtime overhead?
[07:06] Priya: quantized kernels are generated ahead of time for the profile; runtime selects kernels, so startup cost is small. the heavy work is an optional offline calibration pass where we compute scales per-layer — that can take minutes. the runtime then uses fast int8/fp8 kernels with little overhead.
[07:24] Rina: and does this affect streaming or function calling?
[07:28] Priya: streaming is supported; we keep KV cache semantics intact. small caveat: extremely low precision can sometimes slightly change tokenization boundaries in rare edge cases — we've seen this with certain tokenizers, so we recommend eval hooks if you have strict downstream parsing.
[07:47] [07:50] Carlos: competitor question — some teams look at Replicate or running custom ops on SageMaker, any clear tradeoffs?
[07:57] Liam: replicate offers model hosting but not the same production routing and optimize toolkit. SageMaker gives flexibility but you end up building the rollout/monitoring layer — Redwood provides that out-of-the-box plus quantization profiles and cost analytics.
[08:10] Ava: on compliance — do you keep audit logs for who changed profiles and runbooks?
[08:16] Jess: yes, RBAC and audit trails for config changes, plus optional longer retention. we'll include sample screenshots in the security doc.
[08:26] Priya: quick note about terminology — you'll sometimes see "int8-uint8" or "int8-sym" in our logs; the console shows friendly names but exported logs are more granular.
[08:37] Rina: can the optimize page export the config as IaC? we'd like terraform.
[08:42] Priya: yes there's an export button — you can export as YAML/JSON and we have terraform modules for Dedicated/Private.
[08:50] Carlos: what's the estimated cost delta for int8 vs fp32?
[08:54] Liam: cost per-token drops roughly proportional to GPU utilization, think 20-40% saving depending on batch and model. we'll put precise numbers in the benchmarking spreadsheet.
[09:05] [09:07] Priya: moving on, here's the regression alert UI — if a profile causes >X% drop on your eval set, we send an alert and can auto-rollback. you can hook Slack or PagerDuty.
[09:18] Jamal: nice. any known gotchas for financial PII data?
[09:22] Jess: for sensitive data we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys, and disable logs or redact sensitive fields before sending. we also support VPC-only egress.
[09:34] Rina: one more technical — does quantization affect prompt ordering / deterministic outputs? we need deterministic classification for audits.
[09:42] Priya: deterministic behavior is mostly preserved, but very low precision could increase variance. we suggest running a determinism check in the benchmark; if it's an issue, use safety profile that keeps critical ops at higher precision.
[09:56] [10:00] Carlos: next steps recap?
[10:02] Liam: we'll send the security pack and SOC2, you will provide the 1k prompt set, Priya will run the three-profile benchmark, and we'll reconvene next week to review results.
[10:14] Rina: timeframe ok — we aim to have prompts by Tue EOD.
[10:18] Priya: great, i'll schedule the job and share the spreadsheet.
[10:22] Jess: also sending pricing for Dedicated + Optimize add-on.
[10:25] Carlos: thanks all, this was helpful.
[10:28] Liam: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[10:33] [END]
